draft.title: Signs of a chemical reaction
card: Some changes give clues that a chemical reaction has happened. These clues are signs that a new substance may have formed.
Common signs are gas bubbles, a new solid called a precipitate, a colour change, light given off, and a temperature change.
A sign only suggests a reaction. It is not proof, because some physical changes also show one. Boiling water makes bubbles, but they are just water vapour.
The best evidence is a new substance with different properties. Look for a sign that cannot be explained by a change of state or by dissolving.
draft.remember: Bubbles, a precipitate, a colour change, light or a temperature change suggest a reaction, but check that a new substance formed.

a.q: Two clear liquids are mixed in a beaker. A cloudy white solid slowly sinks to the bottom. What is this solid called, and what does it suggest?
opts: A precipitate, which suggests a chemical reaction
A precipitate, which suggests a physical change
A solute, which suggests a chemical reaction
A solute, which suggests a physical change
a.why: A new solid that forms when two liquids are mixed is a precipitate, and it is a sign of a chemical reaction. A solute is a substance that dissolves, so it does not appear as a new solid.
a.clue: A new solid has appeared from two liquids.

b.q: Liam heats a pot of water on the stove and sees bubbles rising. Mia adds a tablet to water and sees bubbles rising. Which statement is best?
opts: Mia's bubbles suggest a reaction, but Liam's may not
Both sets of bubbles prove a chemical reaction happened
Neither set of bubbles can ever suggest a reaction
Liam's bubbles suggest a reaction, but Mia's may not
b.why: Boiling water makes bubbles of water vapour, which is a change of state and a physical change. A tablet making bubbles when added to water suggests a new gas may be forming. Bubbles are a sign, not proof, so each case needs checking.
b.clue: Ask what the bubbles in each case are made of.

a.best: A precipitate, which suggests a chemical reaction

b.best: Mia's bubbles suggest a reaction, but Liam's may not
